function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has fascinated humans for millennia. Here’s a quick overview of some key figures who helped uncover its secrets:

| Era | Person | Contribution |
|-----|--------|--------------|
| **Ancient Greece** | **Thales of Miletus** (c. 600 BCE) | Noticed static electricity by rubbing amber (Greek *elektron*). |
| **16th–17th Century** | **William Gilbert** (1544–1603) | Published *De Magnete* (1600), distinguishing magnetism from static electricity and coined the term “electricus.” |
| **18th Century** | **Benjamin Franklin** (1706–1790) | Conducted the famous kite experiment (1752), demonstrating that lightning is electrical. |
| **Late 18th Century** | **Alessandro Volta** (1745–1827) | Invented the voltaic pile (1821), the first chemical battery, providing a steady electric current. |
| **19th Century** | **Michael Faraday** (1791–1867) | Discovered electromagnetic induction (1831), laying the groundwork for electric generators. |
| **19th Century** | **James Clerk Maxwell** (1831–1879) | Unified electricity and magnetism into Maxwell’s equations (1860s). |

So while no single person “discovered” electricity, it was gradually understood through the work of many scientists over centuries.
